'''Eivind Hiis Hauge''' (born 15 November 1937) is a Norwegian physicist.

== Early life and career ==
Hauge was born in [[Bergen]],<ref name="snl">{{cite encyclopedia|year=2007|title=Eivind Hiis Hauge|encyclopedia=[[Store norske leksikon]]|editor=Henriksen, Petter|publisher=Kunnskapsforlaget|location=Oslo|url=http://www.snl.no/Eivind_Hiis_Hauge|language=Norwegian|accessdate=26 May 2009}}</ref> but took his secondary education at [[Oslo katedralskole|Oslo Cathedral School]].<ref name="Forskning">{{cite news|url=http://forskningsradet.ravn.no/bibliotek/forskning/200203/200203013.html|title=Tåler kjeft|date=March 2002|work=Bladet Forskning|first=Siw Ellen|last=Jakobsen|language=Norwegian|accessdate=26 May 2009|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071108003816/http://forskningsradet.ravn.no/bibliotek/forskning/200203/200203013.html|archivedate=8 November 2007}}</ref> He then took the [[sivilingeniør|siv.ing.]] degree, graduating from the [[Norwegian Institute of Technology]] in 1962 and took the dr.techn. degree in 1965.<ref name="snl" /> He spent the years 1965 to 1967 as a research fellow at [[Rockefeller University]]. He was a professor of [[theoretical physics]] at the Norwegian Institute of Technology from 1976.<ref name="Forskning" />

In 2001, having been [[dean (academic)|dean]] of the Faculty of Information Technology, Mathematics and Electrical Engineering, he ran for election as [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]], the successor of the Institute of Technology. He chose Julie Feilberg as his vice rector candidate, and they edged out the other candidates Kathrine Skretting and Ingvald Strømmen.<ref name=valg>{{cite news|title=Hauge/Feilberg vant rektorvalget ved NTNU|date=6 November 2001|work=Adresseavisen|pages=2|language=Norwegian}}</ref> He assumed the rector chair in 2002.<ref name=snl/> In the summer of 2005 his period ended, and he was succeeded by [[Torbjørn Digernes]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.universitetsavisa.no/ua_lesmer.php?kategori=nyheter&dokid=42ea18b931b3b0.49642719 |title=Hauges siste rektordager |date=28 July 2005 |work=Universitetsavisa |first=Tore |last=Hugubakken |language=Norwegian |accessdate=26 May 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723183847/http://www.universitetsavisa.no/ua_lesmer.php?kategori=nyheter&dokid=42ea18b931b3b0.49642719 |archivedate=23 July 2011 }}</ref>

He has been the chair of [[Trondheim Symphony Orchestra]] and the [[Trondheim Soloists]], and a board member of the [[Nansen Academy]].<ref name=valg/> He is a member the [[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntva.no/index.php?option=com_club&view=member&id=177%3Ahauge-eivind-hiis&Itemid=60|title=Medlemmer: HAUGE, Eivind Hiis|publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences]]|language=Norwegian|accessdate=27 June 2013}}</ref> In 2006 he was decorated as a Commander of the [[Royal Norwegian Order of St. Olav]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.universitetsavisa.no/ua_lesmer.php?kategori=nyheter&dokid=446d5b69b975c3.20058530 |title=Hiis Hauge hedret med St Olav |date=18 May 2006 |work=Universitetsavisa |first=Arne |last=Asphjell |language=Norwegian |accessdate=26 May 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723183909/http://www.universitetsavisa.no/ua_lesmer.php?kategori=nyheter&dokid=446d5b69b975c3.20058530 |archivedate=23 July 2011 }}</ref>
